statement: The following facts hold. 1. Let (u, K) be a reduced, rectifiable absolute minimizer of the fidelity functional in an open set Ω ⊂ R2, with bounded fidelity datum and locally bounded u. For each x ∈ K and each sequence rj ↓ 0, a subsequence of Kj = K − x rj , uj(y) = u(x + rjy) √ rj 8 on the expanding domains (Ω − x)/rj has a global generalized limit (v, H, {pkl}). The sets converge locally in the bilateral Hausdorff sense. The set H is closed, rectifiable, locally of finite length, and is the support of H1⌞H; moreover 0 ∈ H. For every bounded open D ⋐ R2, v ∈ W1,2(D \ H). 2. If a global generalized minimizer has connected complement D = R2 \ H, then (v, H) is an absolute minimizer of the homogeneous energy E0 under every compactly supported change. In particular, changes whose support meets H are allowed. 3. Every global generalized minimizer has a reduced, closed, rectifiable set H of locally finite length, and v ∈ W1,2(D\H) for every bounded open D ⋐ R2. There are positive dimensional constants c, C such that cr ≤ H1 (H ∩ Br(y)) ≤ Cr (y ∈ H, r > 0), Z BR\H |∇v|2 dx ≤ 2πR (R > 0). Almost every point of H with respect to H1 has a neighborhood in which the entire set is a single C1 arc. 4. A global generalized minimizer has at most one unbounded connected component of its closed set. If its closed set disconnects the plane, that set is a line or three half-lines meeting at 120 degrees. If all but at most one connected component of its closed set lie in one compact set, the set is empty, a line, three half-lines meeting at 120 degrees, or a half-line. 5. There are α ∈ (0, 1) and ε > 0 with the following property, with the constants chosen for the fixed bounds on the fidelity datum. Suppose that a reduced absolute minimizer is defined in a neighborhood of B2s(x), where s ≤ 1. If its closed set in B2s(x) has bilateral Hausdorff distance less than εs from a diameter, a radius, or three radii meeting at 120 degrees, then its entire intersection with Bs(x) is C1,α-diffeomorphic to that model. Any three arcs meeting in the smaller ball meet at 120 degrees. The endpoint or junction in this conclusion need not be the original center x.
